thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty fired: P1 — Redis client connections > 95% on cache-prod-us-east. Pager: db-pager. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/redis-conn-surge

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident created: https://pd.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-1987654329 — auto-notify oncall

Maya (oncall): acked — I'm on it, will triage and coordinate.

Jonas (sre): jumping on this. Observed sustained p99 latency ~2.8s for GETs, error rate increasing. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/redis/cache-prod-us-east?panel=conn

Priya (db): seeing repeated log lines on 3/5 primaries: `-ERR max number of clients reached` and clients being closed. App errors show `503` from cache layer, some downstream writes falling back to DB synchronously.

Maya (oncall): what services are causing the most connections?

Jonas (sre): looks like backlog from `ingest-high` job workers — they started a retry storm after a downstream timeout. Connections/time series attached: `ingest-high` peaked 9k concurrent conns to Redis cluster.

Priya (db): Postgres pools also creeping up because some requests fall through to DB. We have pgbouncer at capacity on app-db-prod-1. Risk of cascading DB failure if we continue.

Luis (platform): I'm preparing to add a redis node to the cluster -- provisioning vm and joining to cluster. That will take ~4-6m + rebalance. Prefer short-term mitigations first.

Maya (oncall): short-term plan: 1) throttle job queue (pause or scale down workers); 2) apply config bump if safe; 3) enable read-only fallback for non-critical endpoints; 4) start node add as warm path.

Maya (oncall): I'm going to pause the ingest queue now.

Support (ops): FYI support dashboard shows ~320 affected accounts with increased error rates, mostly non-enterprise. Communicating to CS.

Jonas (sre): pausing workers. Command run: ```
kubectl -n jobs scale deployment ingest-high-workers --replicas=2
```

Jonas (sre): API confirms scaled down to 2 replicas, connections dropped ~70% within 45s. Metric: `redis.clients.connected` fell from 9200 -> 2600.

Priya (db): we still see `ERR max number of clients reached` intermittently on two primaries. We can try `CONFIG SET maxclients` as a temporary relief, but that may just be a band-aid. Rolling restart would be needed for full config changes.

Luis (platform): I'm going to prepare the new redis instance anyway. Starting instance: `cloudctl instance create redis-node-a --zone us-east-1 --type r6g.large`

Priya (db): trying `CONFIG SET maxclients 10000` on affected master (ssh to redis-node-3): ```
redis-cli -h 10.2.3.12 -p 6379 CONFIG SET maxclients 10000
# output
OK
```

Jonas (sre): after config change, client rejections dropped but latency still elevated at p99 ~1.2s. Good improvement, but we should avoid relying on config alone.

Maya (oncall): Customer impact summary so far: ~4% of API requests seeing cache errors, ~0.8% encountering end-to-end 503s. Estimated customer-visible errors: ~320 accounts, mostly short-lived. No data loss reported.

Support (ops): posting update to incident channel and CS channel: "We are mitigating a Redis client connection surge. Some customers may see transient errors. Engineers are throttling background jobs and adding capacity." :thumbsup:

Luis (platform): new node joined cluster and rebalance started. Logs: ```
redis-trib rebalance -> migrating slots 0/16384 ...
```

Jonas (sre): monitoring p99, traffic shaping is holding. Also set emergency circuit on non-critical writes to drop to read-only for 10m. Command: ```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/featureflags/readonly-fallback -d '{"duration_m":10}'
```

Priya (db): pgbouncer pools reported some spike but remain under max after worker throttle. Watching DB error logs for any signs of saturation.

Maya (oncall): Posting status update to #incidents and #customer-facing: "Incident: Redis client connection surge, mitigation applied (job throttle + config bump + capacity add). Monitoring for recovery. ETA next update 10m."

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-1987654329 acknowledged by Maya (oncall).

Jonas (sre): Starting tail on app logs to ensure no new error patterns: ```
stern api-prod --since 10m | grep -i "ERR max number of clients reached" -n
```

(10m passes)

Jonas (sre): No new `max number of clients` since throttle + config + new node. Error rate back to baseline ~0.3%. p99 latency back to ~110ms.

Maya (oncall): Great. I'll hand this to Priya for post-incident follow-up and writeup. Leaving pager open for 30m of quiet.

Priya (db): taking handoff for RCA. Preliminary notes: root cause = retry storm from ingest workers + insufficient redis maxclients headroom + reactive fallback to DB increased DB pool pressure. Mitigations = job throttling, temporary config increase, added capacity, read-only fallback. Next: schedule postmortem, add auto-throttle in job scheduler and alert tuning for client-conn % rather than absolute thresholds.

Support (ops): CS communicated to affected customers, set status page to "Degraded" for cache layer with note about mitigation in progress.

incident-bot: Monitoring: 30m quiet window started. If no flapping, incident will be transitioned to post-incident review.

Maya (oncall): ack, closing active coordination. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident INC-1987654329 marked as resolved by Maya (oncall).
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread about Redis/Postgres paging and mitigation.
